newsitem.title: PERU: Lima Stock Exchange stirs from lethargy, ends up.
newsitem.headline: Lima Stock Exchange stirs from lethargy, ends up.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange awoke from its recent lethargy to close higher overall Wednesday on a return of foreign investors and growing confidence in the local economy, brokers said.

"Today we have felt a strong presence of foreign investors who are returning to the market due to the attractive prices of some shares and the political confidence shown in the minister's speech," said Guillermo Siles, of Argos brokerage, referring to Economy Minister Jorge Camet's speech to Congress earlier in the day on the 1997 budget.
Analysts predicted continued rises on the bolsa in coming days.
On Wednesday, the General Index .IGRA rose 1.08 percent to 1,450.38 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL gained 1.44 percent to 2,005.45.
Total market volume was a healthy 46.61 million soles ($18.76 million) on 2,471 trades. Overall, 43 stocks rose, 18 fell and 32 were flat.
"Investors have stopped being cautious," added Siles.
Brokers said the wait for the government's announcement of a replacement to recently-resigned Presidency Minister Jaime Yoshiyama had not affected the market.
Mining, brewery and public sector sectors were performing well, they added.

Benchmark Telefonica del Peru accounted for 16.2 percent of total trade, ending off overall 0.17 percent to 5.72 soles. Among other leaders, Backus y Johnston rose 3.53 percent to 2.64 soles on 1.69 million shares, while miner Buenaventura gained 0.48 percent to 21 soles on 217,878 shares.
